pillar_reactions.evidence: He had already validated the mechanism on his own body before the call and volunteered the evidence: 'When I tried this yesterday or the day before yesterday, I tried the kettlebells in my home... I thought I was in shape when I go to the gym. When I did. I'm almost passed out.' He drew his own conclusion from it - 'this like gives you, forms the muscle, this gym machines, but it doesn't give you endurance' - and completed the rep's sentence during the pitch, supplying 'Awaking sleeping muscles' himself. Confirmed after delivery with 'No, no, I really like what I'm just hearing, so I follow it.'

Agreed without questions - 'Yes, sure' and 'Yeah, yeah, totally' - to the no-macro-counting positioning. The reaction is warm but the pillar was delivered blind to what he actually eats. He had already disclosed that he deliberately stays hungry, skips breakfast, eats nothing after 6 or 7pm, and does so because 'when you feel hungry, your organism, it's your fat', and none of that was addressed before or during the nutrition pitch. He is the prospect in the batch with the clearest live nutrition problem and the pillar was not connected to it.

Presented as daily accountability, video form review by Trevor and a community of '120 other members', and accepted without questions or pushback. He had named what he wanted earlier and it matches only partly: 'what to do and what to eat, yeah. That's the main thing.' He asked for instruction rather than accountability, and never indicated that adherence was a problem for him - he has trained three to four times a week for two years unaided.

anchors.raw: And then, yeah, like if there's one other option, which is three months, which is 4K as well.
anchors.note: Proposed label: improvised_short_tier. Presented up front as one of 'three main options' rather than as a concession, which is a change from the previous day when the same tier was introduced the same way to Pat Klaver. The prospect immediately made it the reference point - 'I thought that it would be kind of, minimum is like three months?' - and then evaluated everything against $4,000, so the flagship was effectively out of the conversation the moment the third tier was named.

anchors.raw: for the 4k, I mean, we'd usually start, if we can put down 1500, that would get you into the program and we could do a 30-day, love it or leave it
anchors.note: Proposed label: improvised_entry_point. The final rung of a ladder that ran $6,000, $9,000, $4,000, $199 a month, $1,500 - a drop from the headline figure to the entry figure in roughly four minutes, driven entirely by hesitation with no financial information ever gathered. 'We'd usually start' presents it as routine practice, which nothing else in the batch supports.

anchors.raw: It's $1.99 per month, but you can cancel it whenever you want. You could sign up for the whole year and get like a discount
anchors.competitor: Primal University - the company's own lower tier
anchors.note: Proposed label: internal_downsell_tier. Fourth appearance of this pattern in the batch and the fourth different set of numbers for the same product. Here it arrived mid-descent between the $4,000 tier and the $1,500 entry, so the prospect was shown three different price points inside two minutes.

anchors.raw: I'd rather stay home in the morning and do my workout and then go on with my day rather than go to the gym and da-da-da-da-da-da-da, and seeing every person, every day, same guy, same train, personal stuff
anchors.note: Proposed label: existing_gym_rejected_on_experience. The obvious cheap substitute is one he is actively trying to leave, and for reasons - boredom, crowding, air quality, time - that money does not solve. He also has the equipment situation half-solved already, with a backyard and a kettlebell he has used. There was no competing product in his head, which makes the speed of the price descent harder to justify.

unmet_demand.want: To be told what is actually causing the six-month plateau and the belly fat that will not shift. He said plainly 'I don't know what it is, to be honest.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep never diagnosed it. He asked whether it was the workouts, got a genuine 'I don't know', asked about macros, received a description of self-imposed hunger and fasting, and moved on to the pitch without offering an assessment.

unmet_demand.want: Correction of a mistaken nutrition belief - that being hungry burns fat - which is currently driving him to skip breakfast and stop eating after 6pm while in a self-managed deficit and lifting four times a week.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: It was disclosed in detail and received 'Okay, wow. Hmm.' The programme's nutrition pillar was then presented generically. Nothing in the offer or the process requires the rep to address a live misconception, and this was the single clearest opportunity in the batch to demonstrate expertise for free.

unmet_demand.want: A reason to change beyond boredom - he came looking for one and could not produce it himself.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The playbook assumes a gap exists and offers no path for a prospect who declines to supply one. The rep asked three times and then stopped, and the process has no next move after that.

unmet_demand.want: A price that matches a low-stakes experiment for someone testing whether he likes a new training style.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He was eventually offered one - $1,500 with a 30-day exit - but only after four price points in four minutes, which is more likely to have raised doubt about the value of all of them than to have closed him.
